methodSections.heading: Beef Tenderloin with Spinach, Ricotta Gnocchi and Caramelized Onion Marsala Sauce
steps: Season the beef with salt, pepper, garlic, rosemary and olive oil, and then grill or pan sear until medium rare. Add a slice of the cheese to the top of each steak just before they are done.
Cook the spinach in fry-pan with olive oil, salt and pepper. Cut the eggplant into 2-3cm disks, brush with some oil and grill until soft.

methodSections.heading: Sauce
steps: Finely slice the onion and then cook it with the butter on low heat until soft and sticky; this will take around 10 minutes. Add marsala and demi glaze and season with salt and pepper to taste.

methodSections.heading: Ricotta Cheese
steps: Line a large sieve with a layer of cheese cloth and place over a large bowl.

In a saucepan, slowly bring the milk, cream, buttermilk and salt to a gentle simmer over a medium to low heat. Stir occasionally to prevent scorching until little bubbles form on the surface, this will take around 10 minutes.

Let the mixture bubble gently, without stirring, until temperature reaches 80°C (175°F) on an instant-read thermometer; this will take around another 5 minutes and curds will begin to form. Remove from the heat and let sit, without stirring, for 10 minutes.

Gently pour the mixture, including any bits on the bottom, into the lined sieve. Let drain until all the liquid runs off but the cheese is still moist, about 1 hour. Discard the liquid. Chill the ricotta, covered, until ready to use for up to 2 days.

methodSections.heading: Ricotta Gnocchi
steps: Mix together all the ingredients into a dough. Roll the dough into a log around 2cm thick. Cut the log into 2-3cm lengths. Store the gnocchi on a floured sheet pan in the fridge.

methodSections.heading: Serving Up
steps: Boil the gnocchi in salted water until they all float, then drain. Place the a piece of eggplant in the middle of each plate, add the spinach and on top place the steak. Top with sauce and gnocchi.
